after.description:
All-Star Kandor is a living miniature civilization under Superman’s protection, with residents capable of scientific action and a planned relocation. The best-guess material model is a technically sustained city whose basic support is largely independent of ordinary outside earnings. Guarantees are favorable but bounded by dependence on the protective environment and incomplete household detail. Miniature scale itself is not the production mechanism or a labor statistic.

Control is mixed between resident institutions and a powerful non-AI protector. Superman’s assistance does not prove either equal citizen ownership or autonomous AI sovereignty. The intermediate nonworking estimate allows technical support while counting care, science, civic organization and maintenance as useful activity. It is an all-age humanoid scenario, not a count of which heroes enter Superman’s body. The record is separate from a Brainiac-captive Kandor because the provider relationship and security differ, and it does not import every Superman continuity into one miniature economy.

scope.population: Living Kandorian humanoids; explicit alien-person proxy

after.description:
Kandor’s captive inhabitants survive in a technically maintained miniature environment while an android Brainiac controls its wider conditions. The best-guess material floor keeps bodies alive without implying a freely enforceable right to life, movement or a chosen future. Guarantees therefore lean weak despite continuing maintenance. The point concerns living captives before rescue, not an extinct population or every later version of the city.

Control lies toward autonomous machine authority in this explicitly selected android-Brainiac continuity. Biological or different reboot versions are not averaged into the same score. The intermediate nonworking estimate allows automatic habitat support while retaining useful local care, science, administration and maintenance. It is a humanoid-person scenario with a broad interval, not a percentage inferred from being bottled. The source describes multiple versions, so the specific household rules remain best guesses. The All-Star protected city has a different provider relationship and is recorded separately rather than counted as identical captivity.

after.analysis:
The merged Delamain becomes a more advanced being and leaves Night City. This establishes synthetic autonomy, but not a new resident community or a durable provision arrangement for humans. The city’s ordinary corporate automation already has a retained record.

The best-guess comparison gives strong autonomous control, uncertain resource security and no assumed ongoing useful role for the departing individual. Its one-person participation interval spans zero to one. These are explicit estimates, not a claim that AI development or travel alone creates another post-work society.

after.analysis:
Lamb plans to concentrate residents’ memories in a selfless leader, and the player disrupts that project. The plan is not the same as a completed resource system providing everyday necessities to a new population. Rapture’s actual earlier economy remains separately retained.

The requested best guess for the proposed model favors collective provision under concentrated human-derived authority, with very uncertain participation. Those coordinates are conditional projections of an ideal rather than enacted canon. The object is fully analyzed as a failed proposal and is not counted toward the target of researched societies that actually operate in the fiction or a playable configuration.
